intro: If you've been thinking about converting a tired bathroom into a sleek, accessible wet room, you're not alone — it's one of the most popular bathroom upgrades we're seeing across Borthwickwood right now. Whether you're planning ahead for later life, dealing with limited mobility in the household, or simply want a modern, low-maintenance shower space, a properly installed wet room adds real value and daily comfort. Borthwickwood homes vary enormously in layout and construction, so getting the installation right from the start matters more than most people realise. A good wet room should last decades with minimal fuss — but only if the waterproofing, drainage, and tanking are done properly from day one.
localContext: Borthwickwood sits in Midlothian, and the mix of property types here creates some genuinely varied challenges for wet room installation. Older stone-built properties and period cottages — which make up a good portion of the housing stock — often have thick solid walls, uneven floors, and limited existing drainage infrastructure. These features require more preparation work before any tiling or tanking can begin, particularly when it comes to creating the correct fall to the drain without compromising floor joists or screeding over damp-prone surfaces. Modern estate homes in Borthwickwood tend to be more straightforward, with accessible pipework and level subfloors, though they often have smaller bathrooms that need clever planning. It's also worth noting that Borthwickwood sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale can build up on screens, fixtures, and shower heads over time. Choosing the right sealants and grout — and considering a water softener — can make a real difference to long-term maintenance.
serviceDetail: A full wet room installation in Borthwickwood typically follows a clear sequence of work, and understanding each stage helps you plan realistically. The process begins with a survey of the existing bathroom or shower space, where a tradesperson will assess the floor structure, existing drainage position, and wall construction. In older stone properties, this stage occasionally turns up surprises — historic damp, uneven joists, or pipe runs that need rerouting — so it's important to factor in some contingency time and budget. Once the room is stripped back, the subfloor is prepared and a drainage channel or point drain is installed at the correct gradient. This is arguably the most critical step: the fall must be precise to prevent pooling. The walls and floor are then fully tanked using a specialist waterproof membrane system, which is applied in multiple layers and allowed to cure properly before anything else is fixed. Only after the tanking is signed off does the tiling begin — choosing porcelain or stone tiles with appropriate slip ratings is strongly recommended for safety. Finally, the shower valve, thermostatic controls, screen (if used), and all plumbing connections are fitted and tested. A well-managed installation in Borthwickwood typically takes four to seven working days depending on property type and room size.
pricing: Wet room installation in Borthwickwood generally falls in the range of £6,000 to £12,000 for a complete conversion. Simpler projects in modern estate homes — where floors are level and drainage is accessible — tend to sit toward the lower end. Period cottages and older stone-built properties with solid floors or structural quirks tend to push costs higher, particularly if floor screeding, structural repairs, or extra tanking layers are required. The choice of fixtures and tiles makes a significant difference too: mid-range fittings are well within budget, but premium thermostatic valves, large-format tiles, or heated floors will add to the total. Always get an itemised quote so you know exactly what's included.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Borthwickwood and the surrounding Midlothian area pays dividends on a job like this. Local installers will have worked in the same style of stone-built cottages and period homes that are common here, and they'll know where the typical pitfalls are — whether that's managing damp in solid walls or dealing with quirky drainage layouts. They're also easier to get back if a snag arises after the job is done.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built cottage in Borthwickwood?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — but it requires more preparation than a modern property. Solid floors may need screeding to create the correct drainage fall, and walls should be carefully assessed for damp before tanking begins. It's very achievable, but budget a little extra time and contingency cost compared to a straightforward modern bathroom.

faqs.q: How does the moderately hard water in Borthwickwood affect a wet room?
faqs.a: Hard water causes limescale to build up on tiles, drains, and shower fittings over time. Using epoxy grout rather than standard cement grout helps resist staining, and fitting a water softener can significantly reduce ongoing maintenance. Choosing chrome or brushed nickel fittings also makes cleaning easier in harder water areas like this part of Midlothian.

faqs.q: How long does wet room installation take in Borthwickwood?
faqs.a: Most installations take between four and seven working days from strip-out to completion. Older properties in Borthwickwood can extend this if floor preparation or additional damp-proofing work is needed. It's worth discussing a realistic timeline with your installer before work begins so you can plan accordingly — you'll be without your bathroom for the duration.

faqs.q: Is a wet room a good investment for a smaller Borthwickwood home?
faqs.a: In many cases, yes. Wet rooms can make a smaller bathroom feel more spacious by removing the bulk of a shower tray and enclosure. They also appeal strongly to buyers, particularly as accessibility becomes more important. Given Borthwickwood's mix of property types and the premium nature of the work, a well-installed wet room typically adds meaningful value to the property.
